data.narrative: The student successfully architected and executed a multi-agent parallel sprint using interface-first coordination across comments, mentions, and audit logging. When faced with an interface mismatch where independently correct components failed to communicate, they diagnosed the missing cross-feature data flow contract and closed the gap surgically using a decoupled event-driven glue module, verifying all 5 cross-feature checks and preventing data model drift.

dimension_scores.observation: Constructed high-fidelity interface contracts specifying CREATES, READS, MODIFIES, and DATA SHAPES for 3 independent agents, followed by a targeted glue prompt to wire event subscriptions.
dimension_scores.evidence: Documented full parallel plan in progress/ai-augmented-engineering/module-06-parallel-plan.md with explicit TypeScript schemas and event payload definitions.

dimension_scores.observation: Conducted 3 levels of verification: Level 1 individual feature checks, Level 2 cross-feature integration, and Level 3 conflict detection across migrations and test suites.
dimension_scores.evidence: Diagnosed root cause of missing audit log entries: mismatch between Agent 1 eventBus emissions and Agent 3 HTTP middleware interception.

dimension_scores.observation: Resolved the cross-feature integration gap in a single surgical pass via an event translation glue module without re-running or invalidating the parallel agents' outputs.
dimension_scores.evidence: Zero rework on Agent 1 or Agent 2; bridged the integration gap via direct event subscriptions.

dimension_scores.observation: Articulated why parallel execution demands MORE upfront specification than sequential workflows (sequential builds shared context naturally, whereas parallel requires synthetic interface contracts).
dimension_scores.evidence: Recognized that interface contracts must specify both static data shapes AND dynamic data flows (event bus vs middleware).

dimension_scores.observation: Delivered a fully integrated, conflict-free multi-feature system with unified test coverage and decoupled event-driven audit tracking.
dimension_scores.evidence: All 5 cross-feature checks passed: comments create/update/delete events correctly captured by audit log without schema collisions.

strengths: Rigid contract enforcement: pre-specified data shapes and file boundaries to prevent merge collisions
Fast root-cause diagnosis: recognized communication mechanism divergence (event bus vs middleware)
Surgical glue engineering: bridged component gaps without costly full re-generation
data.recommendation: In future parallel workflows, include explicit inter-module communication protocols directly in the initial interface contracts.

public_evidence.student_action: Defined 3 interface contracts and execution plan for parallel development of Comments, Mentions, and Audit Log.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Specified CREATES/READS/MODIFIES boundaries, TypeScript document shapes, and event-driven integration mappings
public_evidence.ability: Coordinates parallel AI agent execution across shared repositories
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Enables 3x development velocity while eliminating git merge conflicts and schema divergence

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Locked schema and endpoint contracts prior to launching parallel agents
Diagnosed event bus vs middleware mismatch in multi-agent output
Bridged independently built features with event adapter rather than re-prompting from scratch

teaching_approaches.detail: House construction analogy: electricians and plumbers need a shared floor plan so pipes don't run through the breaker panel space

learning_style_signals: responds well to concrete failure scenarios
